MY LEAF STUDIO

Compare Two Leaves

Put two leaves side by side. What is the same? What is different?

Look, then try.

Pick two leaves that look different, such as a wide one and a skinny one, or one smooth and one jagged. Make a rubbing of each on the same sheet so you can look at them together. Talk about the edges: are they smooth like a river or bumpy like a saw? Look at the veins: do they run in a straight line or spread like branches? Size, colour and texture all count. There are no wrong answers when you say what you notice.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

An adult helps with scissors when cutting out rubbings. Collect fallen leaves from the ground, or pick with permission, and brush off dirt and insects. Wash hands after handling leaves. Nothing you find outside goes in your mouth.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

Choose my pair

Draw your two leaves side by side. Make each one look different from the other.

ACTIVITY 2

Same and different

Rub both leaves, then look carefully. Draw or write one thing that is the same and one thing that is different.

ACTIVITY 3

Sort my pile

Rub three more leaves, then group all your rubbings: big with big, jagged with jagged. Draw your groups.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Comparing two things and naming what stays the same and what changes is an early science skill. Describing edges, veins and textures builds a precise vocabulary for looking closely.
